name: Huri
overview: Huri was a male member of the tribe of Gad, identified specifically as the son of Jaroah. His designation as a Gadite situates him within one of the twelve tribes of Israel, highlighting his tribal heritage. Beyond this, the biblical record provides no additional personal details or notable events associated with him.
namesAndTitles: The name Huri means 'linen weaver,' reflecting a common practice in biblical times of names bearing occupational or characteristic meanings. There is no indication that this name was given by God, but it serves as a proper personal name within the biblical genealogies.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Huri was the son of Jaroah and infers that Abihail was his father. These relationships place Huri within a known family line in the tribe of Gad, though no further family details are provided.
scriptureSignificance: Huri's significance lies primarily in his genealogical placement within the tribe of Gad, serving as a link in the lineage recorded in 1 Chronicles 5:14. This genealogical record contributes to the broader biblical narrative by preserving the heritage and tribal identities of Israel. Though not prominent in narrative events, his mention affirms the faithfulness of God's people through generations.
